chunks: Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Safwan, from Ibn Miskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the fasting person use siwak (tooth-stick) with water and fresh wood, tasting it? He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يَجِدُ طَعْمَهُ: Tastes it (referring to the water or wood)
key_terms.يَسْتَاكُ: To use siwak (clean teeth with a twig)

ai.seo_question: Does tasting water or wood while using siwak break the fast?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the incidental taste of water or the fresh siwak stick does not break the fast, distinguishing it from swallowing substantial amounts. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in acts of worship, ensuring that routine hygiene practices do not become burdensome for the fasting individual. The chain of transmission through Safwan and Ibn Miskan underscores the reliability of this specific fiqh detail within the Imami tradition.
